text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's progression from a red spot after a minor trauma, I suspect a condition known as pyoderma gangrenosum. To help confirm this and rule out infection, could you describe the appearance of the ulcer's borders and whether you have experienced any joint pain or recent changes in your bowel habits?

text: The presence of dilated tortuous veins and pitting edema strongly suggests a venous etiology rather than pyoderma gangrenosum. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Duplex_Ultrasound

text: The normal venous ultrasound effectively rules out venous stasis ulcers, so let us reconsider the systemic factors. text: Your recent trip to Wisconsin raises the possibility of a fungal infection like sporotrichosis, though your history of uveitis and Crohn's disease strongly points toward a systemic inflammatory condition like pyoderma gangrenosum or erythema nodosum.
